title: “SEQUENCES OF ASSUMPTIONS: Operations and Methods Involving”
notes: 1993 July 19. Ideonomy. ASSUMPTIONS METHODS Sequential MDS-related. The figure is meant to be a crude (partly symbolic and partly realistic) diagrammatization of how (e.g.) Generic Assumptions do in fact [link to, interact with, modify, form static (transcendental) structures and sets of relationships with, etc] [some and all] other Generic Assumptions [in both the mind (mental processes and structures) and the (virtually) self-existent Ideocosm], and also (and thereby) how they [can, should, and must] [behave in ideonomic [mathematics, methods, computations, applications, and applications]]. In particular, the diagram is intended to suggest, and to help discover (through necessary cognitive play), what [are or may be] peculiar [topologico-geometric, statistical, logical, and set-theoretical] phenomena, processes, operations, operators, structures or connections associated with the [use and development] of such Generic Assumptions; especially in connection with [MDS, artificial neural networks, genetic algorithms, heuristics, training of the mind and the ideonomist himself, etc]. Letters of the alphabet (A, B, C,...) represent Generic Assumptions, or the additional Genera of Assumption development as monadic [loops and processes]. These older Generic Assumptions interact with, modify, imply, be succeeded by, be permitted with, specified, generalized by, elicit, quasi-elicit, instantiate, etc [links, steps, events, or something else, operations, operators, etc]. These [sequences, chains, and series] can go on and on, but they may also be finite, or segments of other types of sequences. Thus BLACK arrows represent backward links to [directly or earlier] antecedent Generic Assumptions from a [later or more forward or direct] modal Assumption (e.g. B→A; or compounded, C→B→A). Another kind of Assumptional (phenomenological) sequence instantly skips intermediate Assumption(s)(nodes). It is shown by means of an ORANGE arrow, as in A→C (sans B). Saltation (or circumvention) may be in either ‘forward’ or ‘backward’ directions. Sequences of Assumptions may also be of the more complex RED arrow type.
